How to read it

Position. Every dot is one star. Stars are ranked by luminosity and laid out along the diagonal: the brightest star sits in the top-left corner, the dimmest in the bottom-right. The thin lines mark luminosity steps (1 L☉ is the Sun).

Position is rank, not value: equal steps across the chart are equal numbers of stars, not equal changes in light.

Size. Dot width follows the logarithm of the star’s radius.

Colour. Blackbody colour of the star’s temperature, from red (cool) to blue-white (hot).

Buttons. Tap a category to show only it, tap more to add; the others stay as faint dots so you see where they sit. “All” resets.

Drag to move, pinch or scroll to zoom, tap a star for its numbers.

Reading the labels

measured Directly observed (an angular diameter turned into a radius with a distance).

derived Calculated from other values, e.g. radius from luminosity and temperature.

visual Luminosity from visible light only, without the infrared or ultraviolet light of very cool or hot stars.

spectroscopic · model fit · literature From the star’s spectrum, a model fit, or a paper.

inferred The catalogue gave no class; it was assigned from the star’s position in temperature and luminosity.
